newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SOCCER-AUSTRALIA GIVE VENABLES WINNING START.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AUSTRALIA GIVE VENABLES WINNING START.

text.p: Australia began a new era under former England coach Terry Venables with a lacklustre 1-0 win against New Zealand in a four-nation tournament on Saturday.
Venables endured a frustrating night as he watched Australia twice hit the woodwork in a largely disjointed display in his first match in charge.
Fullback Matthew Bingley scored the only goal when he beat the off-side trap before rounding New Zealand goalkeeper Jason Batty to slide the ball into an empty net after 25 minutes.
"I always knew we had a lot of work to do if we are going to change things. It was like a derby match and I thought we played reasonably. A win is a win," Venables told reporters later.

"We did some good things but there was a lot we could do better," added the former Barcelona and Tottenham Hotspur coach, who signed an 18-month contract to guide Australia through their 1998 World Cup campaign.
Although the home side created a host of other chances, they were also indebted to goalkeeper Zeljko Kalac, who made two outstanding saves to protect lead.
Kalac, who had a brief spell with Leicester City in England, saved close- range efforts from New Zealand strikers Vaughan Coveny and Darren McLennan.
After a bright start, Australia, a side composed entirely of locally-based players, faded badly in the second half, prompting Venables to jump from the bench to shout at his players.
"We needed to be more ruthless with those early chances but after that the opposition came back into it," Venables said.

New Zealand are Australia's only real challengers in the Oceania qualifying group. The group winners will face a play-off against the fourth best Asian country for a berth in the finals in France next year.
Venables adopted a fluid 3-4-3 formation, abandoning the tactics he employed during his two-year stint with England.
Most of Australia's best players, including Aston Villa goalkeeper Mark Bosnich and Lazio sweeper Paul Okon, are based in Europe.
Venables, whose last match in charge of England was last year's semifinal against Germany in Euro '96, had to contend with a major culture shock in terms of his surrounds.
"It was nice to be back in a dugout," Venables said. "But this one was a bit small, I must say."

Instead of a capacity crowd that watches his last match at Wembley, Venables' new side played in front of 10,496 fans at Lakeside Stadium, the modest home ground of South Melbourne in the national league.
At one corner of the ground, several youngsters kicked a football around on a grass bank that divided two small, concrete terraces.
"All I'm concerned about is what happens on the pitch. The bigger the atmosphere the better it is, for sure. But you can get a good atmosphere in small grounds," Venables said.
In the first match in the tournament, South Korea proved too quick and skilful for a below-strength Norway, winning 1-0 with a goal from striker Kim Do Hoon in the 56th minute.
